text.p: Following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The police are investigating information leaks from the government data bases. POSTIMEES claims the police have several suspects, while EESTI PAEVALEHT named an individual, who is suspected of having leaked the information from a mobile telephone company.

- The Reform Party and Right-wing/Moderate block signed a coalition agreement yesterday and announced some members of the new Tallinn city government. The minority government will have to be approved by the council on Thursday.
- The Customs Department accused the state-owned fuel firm Eesti Kutus of business relations with fuel smuggling firms at a news conference. The company deinies the accusations.
- Annely Ojastu, a disabled athlete and Olympic champion, was elected Woman of the Year by the Estonian Women's Association.
- Shareholders of the Hansatee shipping line between Tallinn and Helsinki are discussing the reorganisation of the ferry service.
- The amended draft law on advertising will reach the parliament in December. If passed, the law will restrict the advertising of alcohol and tobacco.
